verdict.rationale: Lithic's Authorization Stream Access (ASA) delivers each authorization as an HTTP POST to the developer's endpoint, which responds with the approval decision. That covers real-time approve/decline in code. However, the evidence never states the network response time budget or a documented timeout fallback the developer can configure. missing for 10: documented response-time budget, a configurable timeout/stand-in fallback behavior, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can approve or decline each authorization in real time — a webhook or auth-stream endpoint my code answers inside the network's time budget, with a documented timeout fallback I control

citations.quote: ASA requests are delivered as an HTTP POST request during authorization.
Your endpoint should respond with HTTP status 200 and the approval decision
Authorization Stream Access (ASA) provides the ability to make custom transaction approval decisions through an HTTP interface to the ISO 8583 message stream.
